subject.title: fix(discord): add configurable REST API timeout via channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs

question: Should OpenClaw accept `channels.discord.apiTimeoutMs` as a supported Discord config contract, and if so should this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93222 be repaired as the landing base?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not only code repair: adding a public config key creates a long-term compatibility contract, and there are two conflicting branches with different completeness and proof levels.

options.title: Repair the fuller timeout PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93222 as the landing base after conflicts and checks are fixed because it already includes docs, metadata, tests, monitor wiring, and proof.

options.title: Bring this branch to parity
options.body: Keep this PR as the landing base only if it is updated with monitor wiring, generated metadata, docs/UI hints, tests, proof, and a clean rebase.

options.title: Decline the public config knob
options.body: Close both timeout-config branches if maintainers prefer changing internal defaults or retry behavior instead of adding another supported Discord config option.

recommendation.title: Repair the fuller timeout PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93222 as the landing base after conflicts and checks are fixed because it already includes docs, metadata, tests, monitor wiring, and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on the Discord REST client behavior and timeout-related hardening paths.
